_comment: Ground truth for prior-standup.jsonl, hand-written. This is the meeting the demo meeting contradicts: Redis / Sam / the twenty-second on issue #2. Loaded verbatim by extraction.load_fixture_statements('prior-standup'), and used to seed memory before the demo so the conflict judge has a history to judge against.

statements.speaker: Them
statements.claim: Use Redis for the transcript ingestion cache on issue #2, because the team already operates Redis for the queue.
statements.quote: Caching first. I went through the numbers on issue two and Redis is the right call — we already run it for the queue, so it's not a new thing to operate.

statements.speaker: Them
statements.claim: Sam owns the cache layer work because he already knows the ingestion path.
statements.quote: Sam owns it. He's already got the whole ingestion path in his head, so it's the cheapest handoff.

statements.speaker: Them
statements.claim: The cache layer ships on the twenty-second, leaving a week of soak before month end.
statements.quote: Ship the twenty-second. That leaves us a week of soak before the end of the month.

statements.speaker: Them
statements.claim: SHA-5, the streaming adapter, is still in progress: the ingestion path is sketched out but nothing is merged.
statements._comment: The words 'streaming adapter' sit in the SAME segment as SHA-5 on purpose. This statement is what SETTLES the ticket's name in memory, and the demo's progress-report beat snaps to whatever it settles on. An earlier wording put 'interface' in this sentence and seeding christened SHA-5 'interface design' — technically defensible, and wrong on a screen.
statements.quote: SHA-5, the streaming adapter, is still in progress. The ingestion path is sketched out, nothing merged yet.

statements.speaker: Them
statements.claim: The auth migration on issue #1 is on track; the dev environment has authenticated end to end since Tuesday.
statements.quote: Issue one is on track. The dev environment has been authenticating end to end since Tuesday.
